themes_detail.label: Illegal Fireworks Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal fireworks complaints exploded to 21 this week 2 weeks ago vs. a baseline of 0.9 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 2,300% spike (z-score: 25.78)—suggesting either organized activity or a emerging enforcement gap in Bay Ridge/Dyker Heights.
evidence: 21 illegal fireworks complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2,300% increase)
Z-score of 25.78 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Spike is the most severe outlier in entire 311 dataset for this district
reporting_angles: Interview residents on 5th Avenue and nearby blocks about timing, frequency, and impact on sleep/pets
Contact NYPD about enforcement operations and whether they've identified source locations or organized sellers

themes_detail.label: Dead Animals & Park Wildlife Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints jumped to 15 last week vs. 1.8 weekly average (757% spike, z-score: 5.96), while animal-in-park complaints hit 4 this week vs. 0.5 baseline (700% spike, z-score: 4.95)—signaling possible environmental stress, disease, or food source issue affecting wildlife.
evidence: Dead animal complaints: 15 last week vs. 1.8 weekly average (757% increase, z-score: 5.96)
Animal in park complaints: 4 this week vs. 0.5 weekly average (700% increase, z-score: 4.95)
Two converging signals suggest environmental or ecological trigger rather than random events
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks and NYC Health about whether they've identified disease outbreaks, contaminated food sources, or habitat disruption in Bay Ridge parks
Interview Parks Dept. about disposal protocols and whether they've noticed unusual patterns in dead animal locations

themes_detail.label: Building/Use Code Violations Spike
themes_detail.summary: Building/Use complaints surged to 57 two weeks ago vs. 9.9 weekly average (477% spike, z-score: 11.56)—a statistically extreme anomaly that may reflect illegal conversions, unpermitted occupancy, or enforcement crackdown in the district.
evidence: Building/Use complaints: 57 two weeks ago vs. 9.9 weekly average (477% increase, z-score: 11.56)
439 DOB permits filed over last 90 days, with 371 alterations suggesting active construction/conversion activity
Two active ULURP rezonings (9201 4th Ave, 9818 Fort Hamilton Parkway) in pipeline—may indicate transition zone vulnerability
reporting_angles: Obtain DOB violation list for Bay Ridge to map which block clusters have the highest concentration of unpermitted work
Interview DOB enforcement about what triggered the spike—are they cracking down, or did violations accelerate?
Cross-reference spike timing with ULURP application filings to see if developers are pushing envelope ahead of rezoning decisions

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Decay
themes_detail.summary: Missing street signs jumped to 5 complaints two weeks ago vs. 0.8 baseline (567% spike, z-score: 6.43)—a concentrated infrastructure signal suggesting maintenance gap or systematic damage in wayfinding across the district.
evidence: Missing street signs: 5 complaints two weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average (567% increase, z-score: 6.43)
Part of broader infrastructure signals: Noise up 155% and Street Condition ongoing top-10 complaints (420 over 90 days)
Complements recurring CB budget requests for garbage/recycling and street infrastructure
reporting_angles: Walk neighborhoods to photograph missing/damaged signs and map geographic pattern (single corridor vs. citywide?)
Contact NYC DOT about sign replacement backlog and whether Bay Ridge is under-resourced vs. other districts

themes_detail.label: Noise & Residential Disruption
themes_detail.summary: Residential noise complaints surged to 30 last week vs. 11.8 weekly average (155% spike, z-score: 4.72), escalating an already top-10 complaint type (696 over 90 days) and suggesting either new noise source or enforcement lapse.
evidence: Noise complaints: 30 last week vs. 11.8 weekly average (155% increase, z-score: 4.72)
Noise is already top-5 complaint category district-wide (696 complaints over 90 days)
Spike coincides with seasonal (spring/summer) increase in outdoor activity and construction
reporting_angles: Survey residents on which blocks (near 5th Ave? near Shore Pkwy?) are most affected and what times of day
Request NYPD noise enforcement data for Bay Ridge to see if citations increased or decreased during spike week
